nodes.label: 100k-connection burst-absorption gap (68.8% established)
nodes.rationale: asyncio.gather() fires all 100,000 open_connection() calls at once, an instantaneous SYN burst that overwhelms the 1024-deep RX ring's ~32-iteration absorption window before the single busy-poll lcore drains it, even though cycles/packet has ~40-50x steady-state headroom. Candidate fixes: RSS/multi-queue, SYN-cookie backpressure, client-side pacing, dynamic ISN pool.

nodes.label: RX ring depth vs. burst-size ceiling (RX_RING_SIZE=1024 / RX_BURST_SIZE=32)
nodes.norm_label: rx ring depth vs. burst-size ceiling (rx_ring_size=1024 / rx_burst_size=32)
nodes.rationale: The ring absorbs a burst of up to 1024 packets (32 loop-iterations of slack) before imissed starts counting; deepening the ring only delays the drop. This, not per-packet CPU cost, is the actual binding constraint measured at the live 100k run.

nodes.label: Measurement flaws F2-F16 classification
nodes.rationale: Classified 2026-08-08 from the first valid baseline-vs-0-RTT run pair. F2 (netem on server egress making FCT gain unmeasurable) resolved 2026-08-08 by moving emulated WAN to the middle leg; F3 (24KB SSM log truncation) and F4 (dark in-app rdtsc TTFB) remain the highest-severity open items.

nodes.label: loadgen.py paced-arrival load generation
nodes.rationale: Replaced burst asyncio.gather() with connection i scheduled at t0+i/rate on an absolute timeline, so 100k connections become 100,000 independent latency samples instead of one stress event testing SYN service rate.

nodes.label: netem-emulated WAN RTT placement
nodes.rationale: A root qdisc delays egress only; placement on server-egress proves send_unlock but structurally cannot show an FCT win, because ServerNIC must learn the real ISN before client data would otherwise arrive — satisfiable only on the ClientNIC<->ServerNIC leg.

nodes.label: T8 ISN ack-num translation shift scheme
nodes.norm_label: t8 isn ack-num translation shift scheme
nodes.rationale: ClientNIC stamps V (spoofed ISN) into the SYN ack-num field; ServerNIC extracts V, computes delta vs real ISN, buffers client data until the real SYN-ACK arrives, then rewrites seq/ack by the delta. This is why FCT cannot improve under server-egress netem — forwarding data before the real ISN is known would require changing this scheme, not just tuning.

nodes.label: Idea: close the 100k connection-burst gap
nodes.rationale: loadgen.py's asyncio.gather() fires all 100,000 open_connection() calls at once, producing a SYN burst beyond what RX_RING_SIZE/RX_BURST_SIZE absorbs before the single busy-poll lcore drains it; measured cycles_per_packet shows 40-50x steady-state headroom, so this is burst absorption, not per-packet cost.

nodes.label: #20 — 100k-connection scale run (done)

nodes.label: DDoS resistance
nodes.rationale: The 0-RTT design is structurally a spoofing amplifier — ClientNIC answers every SYN with a SYN-ACK before the server agrees, allocating flow-table state per SYN; threat model not yet written.

nodes.label: Infra hand-tailoring — closed
nodes.rationale: Security-group scoping decided to stay narrow (10.1.0.0/16) for Nitro-conntrack performance reasons, not security; conntrack_allowance_exceeded read 0 after the 100k run.

nodes.norm_label: eswitch is not separate hardware, only flow-table entries
